newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols down despite shadow of data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols down despite shadow of data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt futures options were weaker in early afternoon trade on Thursday, despite weakeness in the underlying futures markets and the shadow of upcoming U.S. durable goods data.
U.S. durable goods orders for September, scheduled for release Friday, are forecast to rise 2.0 percent.
Some options dealers said they had expected to see volatility creep up, rather than fall, ahead of the data.
However, one dealer said the market expects the release of the number to be uneventful.
"It's not that big of a number, really," he said.
At 1230 CDT/1730 GMT, implied volatility for December T-bond options was seen at 10.3/10.4 percent compared with 10.5/10.7 percent at the U.S. open, dealers said.
One dealer noted that the softer volatility levels were surprising, on the surface, because T-bond options volatility normally increases as the underlying market sells off.
"Normally that would make volatility increase but nothing's really going on. We're down a little but in the big picture, we're still in the same range," he said.
He also said levels could be somewhat skewed by the fact that traders had begun to discount prices for time decay ahead of Friday's session.
There appeared to be a light downward bias to trade, with some call selling and put buying seen, he said.
The day's largest play was a purchase of 5,000 to 6,000 December 116-00 puts, he said, which are deep in the money.
"It's a very meaningless trade," another dealer said. "It's not an essential trade, it's not a volatility trade, it's some kind of accounting trade."

Implied volatilities for March eurodollar futures options were flat at 14.6 percent at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, dealers said. June at-the-money eurodollar options were down 0.10 percentage point at 16.8 percent.
"We were a little softer in the morning. We saw a little bit of a volatility buying in the March, mainly puts, and I think that helped it a little bit," one dealer said.
Specifically, there was activity in March 93.50 and 94.00 puts and in the March 94.50/94.25 strangle, he said.
